title: PB 235 Rubber (NSIC Rb 02): Characteristics
metaDescription: PB 235 rubber is a rubber variety from Prang Besar. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: PB 235 is a registered rubber variety, also sold or known as NSIC Rb 02. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1999 as NSIC 1999 Rb 02. Prang Besar bred it.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where PB 235 rubber is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Rb 02, this is the same rubber. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [rubber variety finder](/crop-varieties/rubber), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for tree crops](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: 1 to 25 percent tapping cut with veerosis

blocks.text: The pests and diseases that hit rubber fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** About 2,240 to 2,530 kg/ha/yr on virgin bark.
**Fruit:** Pale yellow latex, dry rubber content about 37.7 percent.
Light Oidium and Colletotrichum, about 5.8 percent brown bast.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: straight, vigorous Prang Besar clone that self prunes and forms a closed canopy. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant PB 235 rubber

Rubber clones differ in latex yield and in how they take tapping and wind. Plant budded clones from an accredited nursery. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation in the Philippines](/land-preparation/land-preparation-philippines).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Rb 02 the same as PB 235?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Rb 02 is another name for PB 235, registered as NSIC 1999 Rb 02. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of PB 235?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
